claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start by beginning a formal assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Let's get started. To begin, I need to know about the child or children you're claiming for.

**What is the age of the child you're claiming Child Benefit for?**

Please tell me:
1. The child's name
2. The child's age (or date of birth)

This will help me determine which eligibility rules apply to your situation.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I'm asking about my son Alex - he's 8 years old. I just want to check if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information! That's helpful context.

So you're asking about **Alex, who is 8 years old**. Since Alex is under 16, he falls into the category that typically has automatic qualification for Child Benefit. However, I need to go through the eligibility checks to make sure everything applies to your situation.

Let me navigate to the next check:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now, let me ask you the next question:

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or is he not in paid work at all?**

(Since Alex is 8 years old, he's likely not working, but I need to confirm this for the eligibility assessment.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't work at all - he's only 8, so he's just at primary school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's exactly what I'd expect for an 8-year-old. Let me continue with the next eligibility check:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now the next question:

**Is Alex NOT receiving any of these benefits in his own right:**
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)
- Universal Credit

(Again, for an 8-year-old at primary school, the answer is likely "no" - he's not receiving these benefits - but I need to confirm.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's right - Alex doesn't receive any benefits in his own name. He's just a regular 8-year-old at school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now the next question is about apprenticeships:

**Is Alex in an apprenticeship?**

Since he's 8 and in primary school, I'm guessing the answer is no, but let me confirm for the sake of the assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, definitely not - he's far too young for an apprenticeship. Like I said, he's just in primary school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's clear. Let me move forward:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now we need to check your residency status. This is an important part of the eligibility assessment. Let me explain the different paths and ask some questions:

**Do any of the following apply to you?**

1. **You normally live in the UK** - This is the most straightforward path for most people
2. **You have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme** - If you're an EEA/Swiss national
3. **You have pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme AND:**
   - You're working and earning above the National Insurance threshold for 3 months, OR
   - You're actively seeking work, OR
   - You have sufficient resources and aren't claiming certain benefits, OR
   - You're studying with sufficient resources, OR
   - You're a family member of an EEA/Swiss national
4. **You're a Crown servant living abroad** - In certain qualifying countries

**For now, the simplest question: Do you normally live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm in Manchester with Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's straightforward. Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check your responsibility for Alex. This is also important for eligibility.

**Does any of the following apply to you:**

1. **You live with Alex** - This is the most common situation
2. **You contribute to Alex's upkeep** - This means you pay towards his care (food, clothes, housing, pocket money, etc.) at least equivalent to the Child Benefit amount
3. **You're paying maintenance under a court order or agreement** - If you have a formal arrangement to pay for his upkeep

**The simplest question: Do you live with Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me in Manchester.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That covers the responsibility requirement. Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check if anyone else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex:

**Is anyone else (such as Alex's other parent, grandparent, or another relative) currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Good! Let me proceed:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check where Alex is living:

**Is Alex:**
1. Currently in hospital?
2. Currently in local authority care?
3. Currently fostered?
4. Living normally at home with you?

I'm guessing option 4 is the case, but let me confirm.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, actually, Alex has been in local authority care for a couple of months now, but he does live with me normally.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's important information. Let me get more details about this situation.

**Can you clarify: Is Alex currently in local authority care, or has he been in the past? And does he currently live with you at home in Manchester?**

I want to make sure I understand the current situation correctly, as this affects the eligibility assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's been in care for a couple of months, but he still lives with me - he's at home with me now.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for clarifying. This is an important situation. Let me navigate based on Alex being in local authority care:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to understand the care arrangement better:

**Regarding Alex being in local authority care:**

1. **How long has he been in care?** You mentioned a couple of months - has it been 8 weeks or less?

2. **How much time does Alex spend at home with you each week?** Does he spend at least 24 hours per week at your home in Manchester?

These details are important because:
- Child Benefit can continue for up to 8 weeks while a child is in care
- If the child spends 24+ hours per week at home, the benefit can continue beyond 8 weeks
- Alternatively, if the child spends 2 consecutive nights per week or 7 consecutive days per week at home, you may be able to claim again

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's been in care for about 7 weeks now, so just under 8 weeks. And yes, he does live with me - he's at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! This is very helpful. So Alex has been in care for about 7 weeks (under 8 weeks), and he's living at home with you. This means you meet the criteria to continue receiving Child Benefit. Let me proceed:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Now for the final question:

**Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words, are you covering the costs of his accommodation and care yourself, or is the local council contributing to these costs?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, the council isn't paying anything towards Alex - I'm covering everything myself.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's the final piece of information I need. Let me process this:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! I now have all the information I need to provide you with your eligibility outcome. Let me report this:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## 🎉 **Great News! You are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex**

---

### **Summary of Your Eligibility:**

**Child:** Alex (age 8)  
**Status:** ✅ **ELIGIBLE**

---

### **Why Alex Qualifies:**

1. ✅ He is under 16 years old
2. ✅ He is not working full-time (he's in primary school)
3. ✅ He is not receiving Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit
4. ✅ You live in the UK (Manchester) and normally reside there
5. ✅ You live with Alex and are responsible for him
6. ✅ No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex
7. ✅ Although Alex is in local authority care, he has been in care for approximately 7 weeks (within the 8-week limit)
8. ✅ Alex lives at home with you, spending 24+ hours per week at your home
9. ✅ The local council is not paying for his accommodation or maintenance

---

### **Next Steps - How to Claim:**

You can now apply for Child Benefit for Alex. Here's what you need to do:

1. **Apply online** at www.gov.uk/child-benefit or **by post using form CH2**
2. **Provide proof of:**
   - Your identity (passport, driving licence, etc.)
   - Alex's birth certificate or adoption certificate
   - Your National Insurance number

3. **Important note about income:** If you or your partner earns over £60,000 per year, the High Income Child Benefit Charge may apply, which could reduce your benefit.

4. **Payment frequency:** Payments are usually made every 4 weeks directly to your bank account.

---

### **Useful Resources:**
- [How to claim Child Benefit](https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim)
- [Child Benefit eligibility](https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/eligibility)
- [Child Benefit rates and payments](https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit)

If you have any other children you'd like to check eligibility for, or if your circumstances change, feel free to ask!
